answer: On stable, open the relevant Ryoku Hub page and press **FILES** to see the full user config it writes and the shipped defaults beneath it. Super+E and Ryoku calls to the files role use it immediately. Nautilus is the shipped fallback. This role does not by itself replace the system's `inode/directory` handler.

Fresh unstable installs select it by default; an existing unstable box receives it once, and removing it is respected.

It publishes an MPRIS player, so Ryoku's now-playing widgets and media keys follow it like Spotify, a browser player, or mpv. Ryotunes releases independently, while Ryoku installs and tracks its signed package.

Use the app's own Set as default control when it has one; otherwise run `xdg-mime default <actual-app.desktop> <mime-type>`. Replace the placeholder with the real desktop-file ID. Ryoku doctor preserves user-chosen MIME defaults.

If audio still does not return, run `ryoku doctor --check`, `wpctl status`, and `journalctl --user -b -u pipewire -u pipewire-pulse -u wireplumber --no-pager`, then attach `ryoku doctor --report` to a #help post.

title: Recover a Missing Desktop After First Login
examples: I logged in but there is no bar
the wallpaper is black after installing
applications open but the Ryoku shell is gone
fresh install boots to a plain TTY
nothing draws on my first Ryoku login
answer: Switch to a TTY with Ctrl+Alt+F2, log in, then run `ryoku reload` and inspect `~/.local/state/ryoku-shell.log`. Next run `ryoku doctor --check`; if it identifies supported drift, run `ryoku doctor`. Use `ryoku recovery` only if update, reload, Doctor, and snapshot rollback cannot restore the packaged desktop, because recovery overwrites Ryoku-managed configs.

title: Prepare Secure Boot for Installation
examples: does Secure Boot need to be off
the installer confirmation will not continue
can I boot the Ryoku ISO with Secure Boot enabled
is TPM the same requirement as Secure Boot
what firmware setting blocks the installer
answer: For the ISO, open your firmware setup and turn **Secure Boot** off, then boot the USB in UEFI mode. TPM is a different feature and does not need to be disabled. The in-place script can run on an existing system, but enforcing Secure Boot on Arch prevents Ryoku from enabling unsigned NVIDIA DKMS modules; sign them with `sbctl` or disable Secure Boot before selecting that driver path.

title: Fix an ISO That Will Not Boot
examples: Ryoku drops back to the Ventoy menu
the ISO flashes black and will not start
how should I write the installer USB
could my downloaded image be corrupted
Ventoy no arranca la ISO de Ryoku
answer: First verify the ISO signature and checksum, disable Secure Boot, and boot in UEFI mode. Stable supports Ventoy: try normal mode first; if it returns to the menu or cannot find the medium, use Ventoy's **GRUB2 mode** from the secondary menu (`Ctrl+r`). If firmware still rejects Ventoy, write the ISO directly with balenaEtcher, `dd`, or Rufus in DD mode. Capture the exact boot error and hardware details if the verified direct-write image also fails.

This controls inserting the current primary selection when you press the wheel; it is separate from Super+V clipboard history and from Emulate middle click. title: Understand Compositor-Specific Features
examples: does niri have the same settings as Hyprland
why did a Hub option disappear after switching
which features are Hyprland only
will my keybinds work on Wayfire
does niri support Hyprland plugins
qual compositor tem todos os efeitos
answer: Ryoku Hub shows controls the running compositor's provider can honor. Stable Hyprland and niri both expose shared pages such as Animations and Performance, but each page hides or disables options its provider cannot apply. Compositor Plugins are Hyprland-only; niri instead exposes its native overview and column behavior. Keybinds stay top-level and carry across where the action is supported. Unstable Wayfire follows the same capability-gated rule, and switch preview lists anything it cannot express.

title: Keep Compositor Overrides Across Updates
examples: Ryoku update erased my Hyprland changes
where should custom niri KDL go
how do I keep raw compositor settings
my user.lua edits keep reverting
which Wayfire file is safe to customize
como manter minhas configurações após atualizar
answer: Use Ryoku Hub for every exposed setting. For a raw setting the GUI cannot express, open the **FILES** chip on a compositor-owned Hub page; it lists the running provider's user-owned files. Stable loads `~/.config/hypr/user.lua` or `~/.config/niri/user.kdl` last. Never edit generated `settings.lua`, `settings.kdl`, `rebinds.*`, `/usr/share/ryoku`, or Quickshell files—updates rewrite them. Unstable Wayfire uses `~/.config/wayfire/user.ini`.

title: Switch Between Hyprland, Niri and Wayfire
examples: how do I switch from Hyprland to niri
where is the compositor picker
can Ryoku install Wayfire for me

answer: Open Ryoku Hub > Window Manager > Compositor, choose a target, review what carries over and press Switch. Ryoku installs it if needed; keeping the old compositor is the reversible default. The current session does not change. Log out, then select the new session at the greeter. Stable offers Hyprland and niri; unstable also offers Wayfire. If a target is absent, its package/provider is not available on that channel—do not install it around the Hub.

title: Deploy Custom Work from a Ryoku Checkout
examples: I changed QML in a clone; how do I run it?
what is the contributor deploy command?
why does ryoku deploy ask for RYOKU_REPO?
should a feature branch use materialize?
how do I put checkout changes on my dev machine?
can I hot-reload without replacing my config?
answer: Check `git status --short` in the checkout first. For a full live deploy, run `RYOKU_REPO=$PWD ryoku deploy` from its root; it builds the owned binaries and lays that checkout into `~/.config`. Keep work on a feature branch, not a channel branch. For shell-only iteration without touching your config, use `ryoku/shell/dev-run.sh` and stop it with `dev-stop.sh`. `ryoku materialize` is for packaged installs.

title: Fork and Reuse Ryoku Under GPLv3
examples: can I fork Ryoku to learn from it?
what license covers the project?
may I publish a modified Ryoku build?
what notices must a fork preserve?
can I reuse code from a Ryoku app?
what are the redistribution obligations?
answer: Ryoku is released under GNU GPLv3, so you may study, fork, modify, and redistribute it under that license. A distributed modified build must meet GPL source and license obligations. Keep the repository's `LICENSE` and applicable `NOTICE` credits, including third-party attribution for adapted portions. A pull request back to Ryoku follows the normal contribution workflow; a private learning fork does not need a separate application.

title: Materialize Config on a Packaged Ryoku Install
examples: how do I re-lay the shipped config on an installed box?
is materialize for packages or source checkouts?
how can I test what a packaged user receives?
does materialize apply user_edits afterward?
what is the packaged equivalent of deploy?
will hand-copying config prove delivery?
answer: Run `ryoku status` first. On a packaged install, `ryoku materialize` re-lays `/usr/share/ryoku/config` into `~/.config` and applies `~/.config/ryoku/user_edits` last. It changes the live config. It is not the dev-checkout command: use `RYOKU_REPO=/path/to/checkout ryoku deploy` for source work. `RYOKU_CONFIG_BASE` is only for deliberately testing another base tree.

title: Open a Ryoku Pull Request
examples: how do I become a Ryoku contributor?

what must be included with a code change?

answer: There is no contributor application: fork `github.com/Ryoku-dev/ryoku`, branch from the current development branch, and make one focused change. Follow `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`, update the matching changelog, verify the behavior on a running system, and let every git hook run. Open the pull request with a concise description of what changed and exactly how you tested it.

title: Verify a Ryoku Contribution Before Commit
examples: what should I test before opening a PR?
how do contributors check QML changes?
which gate proves config reaches installed users?
is parsing enough for a shell change?
how do I dry-run installer work?
can I bypass a failing git hook?
answer: Test the real behavior on a running Ryoku system after the appropriate dev run or deploy; parsing alone is not enough. Run the matching checks from `CONTRIBUTING.md`: `luac -p` for Lua, `bash -n` for shell, `qmllint` for QML when available, and the relevant Go module checks. Installer work has a documented `RYOKU_DRYRUN=1` matrix. Run `bin/ryoku-dev-verify-delivery` for shipped changes and never bypass the hooks with `--no-verify`.

title: Build and Validate Your Own Ryoku Plugin

Supported hosts are `topbarGlyph`, `desktopWidget` and `framePopout`; declare only the hosts the plugin implements. Run `ryoku plugin validate <path>` before installing or sharing it. The plugin guide covers the manifest, settings API, security rules, local installation and RyoStore submission.

title: Choose Arch, CachyOS, or the CachyOS Layer
examples: should I download the Arch or CachyOS ISO
can plain Arch use the Cachy kernel
what is different about the CachyOS edition
is CachyOS worth it for gaming
which Ryoku base is best for an older CPU
answer: Choose the stable Arch ISO for stock Arch userland and broad CPU compatibility. Choose the stable CachyOS ISO for the full CachyOS layer: CachyOS repositories and userland, `linux-cachyos`, tuning, schedulers, and Proton, with stock `linux` kept as a boot fallback. On stable, an Arch install can later add the **CachyOS Kernel** RyoStore bundle, but there is no Arch-ISO layer choice. Unstable adds an optional full CachyOS layer to the Arch installer and RyoStore.

title: Handle the CachyOS x86-64-v3 Requirement
examples: my CPU ISA level is below the requirement
why did CachyOS reject my older processor
can I use the CachyOS layer without x86-64-v3
which edition works on pre-2015 CPUs
the Cachy package lane will not install
answer: The stable CachyOS edition does not require x86-64-v3: its ISO uses generic x86-64 packages, then enables optimized v3 repositories only when the CPU supports them. The separate **CachyOS Kernel** bundle for a stable Arch install is v3-only and refuses safely on an older CPU; keep the stock Arch kernel there. On unstable, the optional full CachyOS layer offered from the Arch installer is also skipped on a non-v3 CPU, while the CachyOS edition itself remains compatible.

title: Choose a Supported Ryoku Edition
examples: which Linux bases does Ryoku support
is there a Fedora edition now
can I install Ryoku on Void
does Ryoku support Artix or Pop OS
which editions have an official ISO
is Ryoku its own distro or built on another one?
what distributions can run the Ryoku desktop?
answer: Stable ships signed Arch and CachyOS ISOs and supports in-place installation on x86_64 Arch-based or Debian-based systems. Its desktop providers are Hyprland and niri; stable does not support Void, Fedora, or Wayfire. On unstable, native editions expand to Arch, CachyOS, Void glibc, and Fedora 44/45: Void is niri-only and has its own ISO, Fedora is script-installer only, and Wayfire is experimental on Arch and CachyOS. NixOS, Artix, and rpm-ostree Fedora remain unsupported.

title: Use Ryoku Game Mode
examples: Does Ryoku have a game booster?

Can Game Mode reduce Wi-Fi latency?
Why does Game Mode refuse on battery?
Will it restore my desktop afterward?
Existe modo de jogo no Ryoku?
answer: Use the `Game Mode` tile in Super+Esc. It is AC-only: while enabled it selects the Performance power profile, reduces latency-oriented system and Wi-Fi power saving, and—where the compositor supports live changes—strips costly decoration and uses fullscreen-only VRR. Turning it off restores the prior profile and saved system state. If the tile reports a failure, run `ryoku doctor --check` before changing power tools manually.

title: Install Steam and the Gaming Bundle
examples: Where do I install Steam in Ryoku?
Does the Gaming bundle include controller support?
How do I get Wine and Proton?
Will NVIDIA games have 32-bit drivers?

answer: Open RyoStore from the launcher, or `Ryoku Hub > Add-ons > Browse RyoStore`, and install the `Gaming` bundle. It brings launchers, Wine and Proton, overlays, controller support, emulators, multilib, and the matching 32-bit GPU userspace. Steam is an item inside that bundle, so it can also be installed alone. Let Steam complete its own first launch before judging its library or shader state.

title: Diagnose Steam Not Launching
examples: Steam will not open after installation
Steam starts in terminal but not launcher
The desktop icon shows an XWayland error
Steam broke after a fresh setup
How do I collect a useful Steam failure log?
Steam não abre pelo lançador

title: Fix Gray or Opaque Blur on Niri

answer: Ryoku deliberately leaves global window blur off on niri 26.04 because niri's forced background effect makes translucent windows opaque instead of frosted. Global blur and X-ray controls under `Ryoku Hub > Window Manager > Look` are therefore unavailable or reported unhonored on niri. Per-app blur remains available at `Ryoku Hub > App Overrides`, and layer-surface blur at `Ryoku Hub > Layer Rules`. Do not force a matchless global blur rule in `user.kdl`.

answer: Turn on Advanced, then open `Ryoku Hub > Window Rules > Rule editor` on stable. Match the real app id/class or title, not its friendly menu name.
